quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles go first. This includes police cars, fire engines, and ambulances using sirens or horns with flashing red or blue lights. Listen to instructions from their loudspeakers. Multiple emergency vehicles often travel together, so wait until the way is completely clear before you move.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. Expect to see bicyclists in the left lane when they are turning left.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower and weaker.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes rapidly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if a tire blows out. Hold the steering wheel tight and take your foot off the gas to let the car slow down. Gently tap the brakes when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until your car has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Big vehicles have bigger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that the driver cannot see in the mirrors.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: It is summer.
You must immediately stop and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to get out of the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They tell you that workers or equipment are on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: If a police officer asks you to take a chemical test and you refuse:

options.text: It is your right and there will be no consequences.
Your license will be suspended.
It is recommended.
You will only get a fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: When you drive in Maine, you agree to take an alcohol test if asked by police. You will not be forced to take the test, but your license will be suspended right away if you refuse.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in a business or residential area is:

options.text: 15 mph.
25 mph.
35 mph.
45 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a business or residential area is 25 miles per hour. Follow any posted signs that show a different speed limit.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass if you cannot see clearly because of a curve or hill. Do not pass at an intersection, on a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in any no passing zone. Never pass a stopped school bus with red flashing lights, unless you are on the opposite side of a multilane road with a median.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a green traffic light?

options.text: Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: When you see a green light, you may continue through the intersection. But first, make sure no vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection. Slow down if needed so you can stop if the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what must you do?

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, you must give the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Wait until the intersection is clear, then complete your turn.

questions.question: What is the main danger shown by this sign?

options.text: Driving with your headlights out of alignment because one side of your car is higher than the other.
Damaging a tire from drifting onto the shoulder.
Hydroplaning, if the shoulder has water on it.
Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto the shoulder, do not brake hard or turn sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and keep your wheels off the pavement. Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Once you are going slow enough, turn the steering wheel gently to get back on the road. Do not jerk the wheel or brake hard.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass. If there is a broken line on the other side, drivers on that side may pass. Sometimes both lines are solid, meaning no one can pass in either direction.

questions.question: When leaving a roundabout or traffic circle, which lane should you be in?

options.text: Be in the left lane.
Honk to alert other drivers to your intentions.
Be in the right lane.
Cut across traffic to reach your exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be in the right lane.
questions.explanation: When exiting a roundabout or traffic circle, you should be in the right lane. Follow road markings and signs if they show a different lane to use.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and keep moving in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, pull to the right side of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Roadwork or maintenance is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roadwork or maintenance is present.
questions.explanation: Orange, diamond-shaped signs warn of construction, maintenance, or utility work ahead. They help drivers and pedestrians stay safe in these dangerous areas. Traffic fines may be doubled in construction zones.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your bloodstream and goes to your brain, where it affects judgment and decision-making first. This makes it unsafe to drive.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs hurt many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, reduce coordination, decrease alertness, and make it harder to concentrate.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, it is hard to see other drivers. What should you turn on to let others know you are there?

options.text: The dashboard lights.
Your parking lights.
Your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers might not see you. Always use low beam headlights when you need your windshield wipers on.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and a siren, you must yield by:

options.text: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
Moving to the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping immediately, even in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle with flashing lights and a siren. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: Bicycles on the road:

options.text: Must always yield to motor vehicles.
Do not have to follow traffic rules.
Are nothing to worry about.
Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are considered vehicles and have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Drivers should respect bicyclists' rights.

questions.question: How often should you have your vehicle inspected?

options.text: Once every four years
Once every three years
Once every two years
Once every year

questions.correctAnswerText: Once every year
questions.explanation: All motor vehicles with a Maine registration must be inspected at an official inspection station once a year before driving on public roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready for a red or yellow light.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low ground railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a low ground railroad crossing. The tracks cross the road at a steep slope. Low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road widens ahead.
The right lane ends soon.
Highway entrance ramp ahead.
The left lane ends soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has flashing red lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and proceed when you think all children have exited.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. You do not need to stop if the bus is on the other side of a divided highway.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them from crossing against the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross safely, even if you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: To merge into a gap in highway traffic, you should:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let other vehicles move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Always check for traffic behind you and to the side before changing lanes. Make sure no vehicles are in your way.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle a full lane when passing. Do not share the same lane. Moving back too soon can force the rider to swerve into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads have less traction than pavement. You must slow down. It takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: You may speed if it is necessary to complete a pass.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Do not pass if you must speed to complete it. Always follow the speed limit.

questions.question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Slowly pass the vehicle at 10 mph or less.
Stop and only move when all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only move when all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk. You cannot see if pedestrians are crossing. Stop and wait until all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You must have enough space between you and the passed vehicle before returning to your lane. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room.

questions.question: Your reaction time slows after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It makes it harder to see clearly and reduces alertness. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and the movement of other vehicles.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Passing cars.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic. You may only turn left when it is safe and does not interfere with oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas pedal or brake to help regain balance. Steer toward the direction of the skid to regain control.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is moving into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to keep your position.
Always keep your current position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room in your lane to allow other vehicles to merge.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means traffic in the lane with the broken line may pass. Traffic in the lane with the solid line may not pass.

questions.question: A five-sided sign is a:

options.text: Stop sign.
Regulatory sign.
School zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers about school zones. It shows where children and pedestrians may cross the street.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you must:

options.text: Drive slowly so vehicles and pedestrians can move out of your way.
Honk your horn so vehicles and pedestrians know you are coming.
Stop first and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop first and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway. Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians. You must stop before crossing the sidewalk. Failing to stop is against the law.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Mainly affect large vehicles only.
Only reduce visibility.
Can affect all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can cause problems for all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility and physically move any vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: Just turn and look over your right shoulder for any lane change.
Look over your right shoulder for right turns and your left shoulder for left turns.
Two outside mirrors mean you have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for right turns and your left shoulder for left turns.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check for blind spots. Make sure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in the next lane.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Move across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough to safely enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in or about to enter a crosswalk. Stay alert for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Cars that are passing.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When you turn left, you must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if you need to.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and check that the way is clear before you go.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other drivers.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By looking in your rearview mirror.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Check them by turning your head and glancing over your shoulders.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The maximum speed limit is 55 mph under good conditions.
You must not drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed limit is 55 mph under good conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for this road. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the passing lane is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians go first.
Speed up as fast as possible.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, you must let any pedestrians or other traffic in the intersection clear the way.

questions.question: Which statement describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: Other drivers will always do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
They expect no help and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being ready to respond to them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves ahead.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If visibility is too bad, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.
